categories.title: 4. Confirmation trains (single-config replay)
categories.blurb: Longer epoch loops that replay a winning Optuna config and report validation + held-out test metrics.

seq_len.short: How many recent 5-min CGM readings the model sees.
seq_len.what: History window length fed into the network.
seq_len.why: Too short misses delayed glucose effects; too long adds noise and cost.
seq_len.effect: 64 ≈ 5.3 hours of context; longer is not automatically better.

depth.short: How many transformer blocks are stacked (shallowness).
depth.why: Depth is capacity. Shallow nets are simpler and often better on small CGM sets.
depth.effect: depth=1 is a short assembly line; deeper stacks can overfit or train slower.

num_heads.short: Parallel attention viewpoints in each block.
num_heads.why: More heads can specialise, but need enough width/data.
num_heads.effect: 1 head is common and stable on small models.

variant.short: Architecture family Optuna chooses (baseline / embed-storkey / forecast-storkey / projection).
variant.what: Which graph wiring to train: where Hopfield memory sits, or baseline (no Hopfield). This is an Optuna categorical choice — each trial gets one architecture from the search space.
variant.why: Placement changes when associative recall can influence features vs the final forecast. Optuna explores variants; it is not fixed by hand per trial.
variant.effect: baseline = pure transformer control. embed-* recalls early; forecast-* recalls late; projection is a lighter linear memory.

hopfield_strength.short: How strongly Hopfield memory mixes into activations.
hopfield_strength.why: Too strong can overwrite useful transformer features; too weak is a no-op.
hopfield_strength.effect: learnable lets training pick the mix; fixed values are easier to compare across trials.

lr.short: Outer Adam learning rate for weight updates.
lr.what: Step size for updating model weights.
lr.why: Too high diverges; too low never improves in budget.
lr.effect: Mid-range ~1e-3–4e-3 often works with champion-like PC settings.

eta_infer.short: Inner PC step size for refining latent beliefs.
eta_infer.what: Learning rate of the PC inference loop.
eta_infer.why: Separate from weight LR — controls how hard latents correct prediction error.
eta_infer.effect: Around 1e-5–2.5e-5 was a healthy band in transformer PC runs.

infer_steps.short: Inner PC iterations per forward pass.
infer_steps.what: How many times latents are refined before forecasting.
infer_steps.why: More steps → tighter energy, more compute.
infer_steps.effect: Low teens (12–18) are typical; doubling rarely helps if η is wrong.

max_infer_norm.short: Clip on PC latent update size.
max_infer_norm.why: Prevents exploding activations on sharp glucose swings.
max_infer_norm.effect: Lower = safer/slower settle; higher = freer but riskier.

grad_clip.why: Stops rare huge gradients from wrecking a run.

lr_decay_epochs.what: Epoch index that starts annealing LR.
lr_decay_epochs.why: Balances exploration early vs fine-tuning later.
lr_decay_epochs.effect: Later decay keeps LR high longer.

weight_init_std.why: Interacts with PC dynamics and depth.
weight_init_std.effect: Smaller often safer with PC; larger can help or explode.

weight_decay.short: L2 penalty that discourages huge weights.
weight_decay.why: On small datasets, unconstrained weights memorise noise.
weight_decay.effect: Higher → stronger regularisation (can underfit). Zero → freer fit.

readout.short: How the sequence is turned into one glucose forecast.
readout.what: Regression head mode: flatten / mean_pool / last.
readout.why: Maps a sequence of vectors to a single 60-min-ahead number.
readout.effect: flatten often best here; mean_pool / last are lighter heads.

seed_offset.short: Seed nudge so similar configs can still differ.
seed_offset.what: Added to the base random seed.
seed_offset.effect: Document the winning seed for fair replay.

energy.short: How PC nodes score prediction error (Gaussian vs Huber).
energy.what: Energy functional used inside PC nodes.
energy.why: Gaussian punishes large errors hard; Huber is more robust to spikes.
energy.effect: Huber can help when a few wild glucose points would dominate.

huber_delta.short: Threshold where Huber switches from quadratic to linear.
huber_delta.what: Delta parameter for Huber energy (only if energy=huber).
huber_delta.why: Controls when an error is treated as an outlier.
huber_delta.effect: Smaller delta → more robust; larger → closer to plain MSE.

ipc.short: Update latents layer-by-layer (incremental PC) vs all at once.
ipc.why: Layerwise updates can improve convergence on deeper stacks.
ipc.effect: On shallow nets the difference may be small.

infer_optimizer.short: Optimiser inside the PC loop: SGD or Adam.
infer_optimizer.what: Which optimiser nudges latent activations during inference.
infer_optimizer.why: SGD is simple/fast; Adam adapts per-coordinate.
infer_optimizer.effect: Try SGD first; Adam if inference looks under-converged.
